draft.title: Hatshepsut
card: Hatshepsut was a woman who ruled Egypt as pharaoh for about 20 years, around 1479 to 1458 BCE. She first ruled for her young stepson, Thutmose III, then took the title of pharaoh herself.
She sent a trade expedition by ship to Punt, a land on the Red Sea coast. It returned with goods such as incense, myrrh trees, ebony and gold.
She built and restored many temples. The best known is her mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari, which shows the Punt expedition on its walls.
Later, many of her statues were broken and her name was chiselled off monuments. Historians think later rulers tried to erase her from the record, but they did not succeed in doing so fully.
draft.remember: Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh, traded with Punt and built temples, yet later rulers tried to erase her name.

a.q: What was the main result of Hatshepsut's expedition to Punt?
opts: It brought back goods such as incense and ebony
It added Punt to Egypt as a new province
It ended a war between Egypt and Punt
It found the source of the Nile river
a.why: The expedition was a trade mission, and it returned with goods such as incense, myrrh trees, ebony and gold. It was not a war or a conquest, so the option about adding Punt as a province is wrong.
a.clue: Think about why ships were sent, and what they carried home.

b.q: Archaeologists find a statue of Hatshepsut that was smashed, and her name chiselled off a wall. What does this best suggest?
opts: Later rulers tried to erase her from Egypt's records
Hatshepsut was never a real ruler of Egypt
Her temples were built by a different pharaoh
Egyptians had no records of any women rulers
b.why: Damage to her statues and name suggests later rulers tried to erase her. It does not show she was unreal: the same temples and records still name her, so the option saying she never ruled is tempting but wrong.
b.clue: Someone chose to remove her name. Why remove the name of someone who did not exist?
